newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate confirms Herman as labor secretary.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate confirms Herman as labor secretary.

text.p: The U.S. Senate confirmed President Clinton's nomination of Alexis Herman as labor secretary Wednesday, ending a standoff over a partisan dispute between Republicans and the White House.

Senate leaders scheduled the confirmation vote moments after a deal was cut under which the Clinton administration agreed to drop a planned executive order on federal construction projects that Republicans and business groups had charged was a payoff to organized labor.

The vote on Herman, 49, who had been director of the White House Office of Public Liaison before her nomination, was 85-13. She succeeds Robert Reich, who left the Labor Department Jan. 12 after four years.

Herman won a unanimous recommendation by the Senate Labor Committee April 10. But Senate Republican leaders halted the confirmation process about two weeks ago after a draft of a proposed presidential order surfaced that admonished agencies to consider so-called project labor agreements for federal construction, which business groups said discriminated against non-union workers and contractors.
Under a deal between Senate Republican leaders and the Clinton administration, the administration agreed to issue a memorandum to federal agencies instead of the executive order.
"Since this is something to encourage agencies rather than be mandatory for agencies, we believe it substantively accomplishes the same goal," said White House spokesman Barry Toiv.
